Over the ten edge ends the mean degree is 2.2; the degrees at the two ends of an edge have covariance -0.64 and variance 0.96, so their correlation is r = -0.667: hubs link to leaves." width="100%"} Degree assortativity measured as the Pearson correlation between the degrees of the two endpoints over all edges (Newman, 2002): positive when hubs link to hubs, negative when hubs link to low-degree nodes. On an undirected graph this equals `assortativity_degree()`; the directed `source_mode=`/`target_mode=` options choose which degree of the source and target to correlate (for example, out-degree of the source against in-degree of the target). Matches NetworkX's `degree_pearson_correlation_coefficient()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source_mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : On directed graphs, the degree of each edge's source: `"out"` (default) or `"in"`. [target_mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["in"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : On directed graphs, the degree of each edge's target: `"in"` (default) or `"out"`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether degrees are weighted. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The correlation coefficient in `[-1, 1]` (NaN if all degrees are equal). ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~assortativity_degree`) : The same coefficient on undirected graphs. [](`~degree_mixing_matrix`) : The table the coefficient summarizes. [](`~assortativity`) : The coefficient for any numeric attribute. ## Examples {.doc-examples} On an undirected graph this is `assortativity_degree()`: ::: {#177036c8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("A", "C"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("D", "F")] ) ( round(graph.degree_pearson_correlation_coefficient(), 3), round(graph.assortativity_degree(), 3), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (-0.667, -0.667) ``` ::: ::: ### Well-cited papers cite well-cited papers `citations()` links each paper of a made-up research field to the earlier papers it cites. By default, the number of papers each paper cites is set against the number of times the papers it cites are cited, and the two are hardly related. Comparing how often the two papers of a citation are cited, with `source_mode="in"`, gives a clear positive correlation: ::: {#4c3024aa .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} papers = ec.citations() [ round(papers.degree_pearson_correlation_coefficient(source, "in"), 2) for source in ["out", "in"] ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [-0.07, 0.36] ``` ::: ::: Sized by how often each paper is cited: ::: {#818479cb .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} cited = {n: papers.get_in_degree(n) for n in papers.get_node_ids()} papers = papers.set_node_attrs("cited", cited) papers.plot(layout="pos", size_by="cited", label_by="label") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
